exposure: Emergency uterine artery embolisation (UAE) after diagnosis by three-dimensional computed tomographic angiography (CTA)
outcome: Avoidance of exploratory laparotomy and/or hysterectomy
cohort: Twelve women who experienced intractable haemorrhage after laparoscopic-assisted myomectomy and were subsequently managed by emergency uterine artery embolisation.
finding: Emergency uterine artery embolisation is a useful minimally invasive option for managing intractable haemorrhage associated with laparoscopic-assisted myomectomy, yielding favorable pregnancy outcomes for women desiring fertility.
mod_finding: All five pregnancies that resulted in live birth were delivered by caesarean section.
